evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Index build/storage wiring covers project-ready full or validation builds, Git incremental rebuilds, IndexSnapshot load, ArcSwap publication, crash recovery, remote fetch cadence, git diff --name-only old_anchor..new_HEAD, and cache-only no-data-loss behavior.

items.impact: A builder must invent ordering, atomicity, rollback, and observable pass/fail behavior for overlapping rebuild, fetch, snapshot-load, mmap, and crash-recovery paths, risking stale or partially published indexes despite the no-data-loss claim.
items.statement: WM-030 names the complete index/storage lifecycle but does not define publication concurrency, corrupted-snapshot handling, recovery precedence, rollback boundaries, or executable failure oracles.
items.title: Index publication recovery semantics remain discretionary

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Route/open reconciliation carries selector precedence, reject rules, closed tab_id vocabulary, scoped resolver rules, route examples, ref-family split, resume_url demotion, Primitive:RouteTarget, OpenSubject, and wrapper/canonical normalization into owner docs and wiring consumers.

items.impact: Implementers can disagree about selector conflicts, rejected combinations, stale tabs, and resume_url normalization unless the referenced owner definitions and wiring fixtures are joined into an executable conformance oracle.
items.statement: WM-031 preserves route/open vocabulary and owner handoff, but this unit contains neither the actual precedence table nor falsifiable examples for valid and rejected selector combinations.
items.title: Route precedence is carried through but not locally falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: GATE-010 must verify route args, wrapper normalization, stale revalidation, admissibility, correlation passthrough, and structured gate-specific evidence for route-aware verification. The Expand Wiring Matrix source wording is preserved as stale/carry-through lineage, not as a new owner schema.

items.impact: GATE-010 may report success while omitting a required check or correlation field because the evidence schema, negative fixtures, and required failure diagnostics are not enumerated here.
items.statement: WM-032 requires structured evidence across six route properties but does not specify evidence fields, per-property pass criteria, or adversarial fixtures.
items.title: GATE-010 evidence completeness lacks an executable contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Timestamp/run/thread fallback logic is compatibility-only inside route/open contracts, and the ref-family split remains explicit when route/open normalization is transferred.

items.impact: A compatibility fallback can silently become the effective canonical resolver, and operators have no stated signal for its use or condition for retiring it.
items.statement: WM-033 correctly labels timestamp/run/thread fallback as compatibility-only but does not state who may activate it, how its use is surfaced, or when it must be removed.
items.title: Compatibility-only fallback has no activation or retirement protocol

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md owns command identity and alias metadata; Wiring Matrix consumes that metadata, still exposes ui_element_id, ui_command_id, handler_location, and expected_event_types, and must not create a second routing schema inside the matrix.

items.impact: The explicit producer-consumer boundary prevents competing command identity and route schemas while retaining the fields wiring validation needs.
items.statement: WM-034 gives UI_Command_Catalog sole ownership of command identity and aliases, makes Wiring Matrix a consumer, and explicitly forbids a second routing schema.
items.title: Command identity ownership boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: tier_runtime_record, tier-keyed usage_record, and tier-keyed evidence_record remain demotion hazards; generated wiring rows must not treat them as canonical producers or consumers until owner-level demotion or replacement is complete.

items.impact: Generation cannot deterministically know when these records become safe to include, so different tools may either block indefinitely or certify stale producer/consumer identities.
items.statement: WM-035 establishes a necessary prohibition but supplies no authoritative, machine-readable demotion or replacement completion condition for generated wiring consumers.
items.title: Runtime-record demotion gate has no completion oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - Wiring_Matrix-S0001 through S0043 remain mapped to fine-grained Wiring Matrix PlanUnits or structural dispositions rather than WM-001.

items.impact: The retired bridge cannot override fine-grained units or masquerade as current implementation coverage.
items.statement: WM-001 is unambiguously retired to generated-tail migration lineage, with fine-grained PlanUnits retaining product coverage.
items.title: Coarse source-preserving bridge retirement is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: targets; wiring implementers must follow the named PlanUnits and referenced

items.impact: Implementers must manually resolve multiple PlanUnits and owner documents, leaving producer, consumer, event, and recovery-action coverage vulnerable to omission or conflicting interpretations.
items.statement: WM-036 establishes that named PlanUnits and Contracts_V0 identities outrank addendum order, but it does not provide a joined, machine-checkable producer-consumer-action map or completeness oracle.
items.title: Runtime wiring consolidation still depends on manual cross-document joins

evidence.exact_quote: Wiring_Matrix binds Assistant Chat Goal Mode command producers to stable command IDs and the Goal Runtime controller. Goal button/chip/icon activation and slash `/goal` dispatch `cmd.chat.goal.start`; Goal status update icon, `/goal again`, and natural-language update requests dispatch `cmd.chat.goal.update`. Wiring uses the Goal Runtime event envelope and does not define concrete Goal event payload schemas.

items.impact: The Goal controls may dispatch during invalid states or fail without a stable disabled reason, receipt, retry behavior, or user-visible recovery path; natural-language update classification is also left open.
items.statement: WM-037 fixes start and update command identities but omits permission, enablement, stale-state, idempotency, receipt, failure, and recovery behavior for each producer surface.
items.title: Goal command IDs are stable but dispatch lifecycle is incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: build define permission, enablement, disabled reason, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, receipt effect, and recovery. Run a doc-impact pass over Assistant Chat, Goal Runtime, Planning Ledger, Plan Document, Plan Compile, Automated Testing, Executor, Orchestrator, Personas, Models, FileSafe, Git/worktree, GitHub, permissions, contracts, commands, GUI, wiring, artifacts, indexes, and reference docs.'

items.impact: A broad prose requirement can be satisfied inconsistently across commands, especially during duplicate delivery, stale projections, activation partial failure, cancel or retry races, and downstream outbox recovery.
items.statement: WM-038 names atomicity, deterministic idempotency, activation, and many command qualities, but supplies no per-command state matrix or executable failure/recovery oracle for the multi-system approval-to-build chain.
items.title: Approval-to-build transaction semantics are not decomposed into falsifiable rows

evidence.exact_quote: - Destination test-send wiring requires explicit user action, enabled destination, masking, rate limit, and receipt recording.

items.impact: Offline delivery, ambiguous send outcomes, credential rotation or deletion, concurrent destination edits, destructive asset operations, and retry deduplication can leak secrets, duplicate notifications, or strand inconsistent state.
items.statement: WM-039 strongly constrains test-send authorization, masking, rate limits, and receipts, but does not specify network-failure recovery, send idempotency, credential lifecycle, delete/restore atomicity, or operator-visible remediation.
items.title: Notification delivery and credential recovery paths remain open

evidence.exact_quote: Production wiring for Usage route/open commands consumes UI_Command_Catalog alias metadata. `cmd.chat.open_thread_usage`, `cmd.chat.focus_thread_usage`, and `cmd.chat.close_thread_usage` are retired compatibility aliases and must not appear as canonical production UICommand rows. Wiring evidence for `cmd.nav.open_usage_subject`, `cmd.artifacts.show_in_usage`, and `cmd.artifacts.show_in_ledger` must prove route_open effect_kind, route_target.object_kind = usage_event when usage_event_ref is present, OpenSubject preservation, and correlation passthrough for usage_event_ref, usage_record_id, provider_attempt_ref, attempt_id, node_id, tool_call_id, trace_ref, receipt refs, raw_payload_ref, artifact_id, run_id, thread_id, source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, settlement_status, projection_freshness, and projection_health where present.

items.impact: Deep links may preserve and expose raw payload, receipt, provider-attempt, trace, and other correlation references without an explicit per-ref authorization, redaction, missing-ref, or expired-ref policy.
items.statement: WM-043 gives an unusually complete correlation-passthrough list and alias prohibition, but the phrase where present leaves sensitive-reference admissibility, redaction, lifecycle, and inaccessible-target GUI behavior undefined.
items.title: Usage correlation preservation lacks privacy and authorization semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Commands with no persisted domain event declare explicit no-persist dispatch or route/open receipts and event-test requirements.

items.impact: The rule prevents fabricated persisted events and makes receipt-only or navigation effects explicit and testable without claiming runtime buildability.
items.statement: WM-042 explicitly distinguishes persisted events from no-persist dispatch and route/open receipts, rejects placeholder events, and binds these distinctions to validation criteria.
items.title: Production wiring effect semantics have a concrete anti-fabrication oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - Provider setup return context routes back to onboarding, Planning Wizard limited state, Health, or the originating Free Models row/list as appropriate.

items.impact: As appropriate permits divergent routing after cancellation, failed auth, lost network, stale return context, app restart, or deleted provider state and can misrepresent readiness or strand keyboard and assistive-technology users.
items.statement: WM-041 fixes the happy-path CTA sequence and false-ready prohibition, but does not enumerate deterministic return routes and recovery transitions for interrupted or failed provider setup, nor accessibility and localized-label command binding.
items.title: Onboarding return context needs an adversarial transition table

evidence.exact_quote: - The Settings toggle writes only enabled or disabled_by_user to the DRY default-guard setting.

items.impact: Rapid concurrent toggles, storage failure after UI optimism, or disclosure refresh failure can leave the setting, receipt, Assistant Chat, and run-detail projections disagreeing about a trust-affecting state.
items.statement: WM-040 closes the state vocabulary and authority boundary but does not define write idempotency, concurrent-update ordering, rollback, or projection convergence and stale-state presentation.
items.title: DRY toggle storage and disclosure refresh lack convergence semantics

segments.summary: Reviewed WM-030 through WM-035 across index publication and recovery, route/open carry-through and gating, compatibility fallback, catalog ownership, and runtime-record demotion. Strong ownership boundaries coexist with missing executable recovery, compatibility-retirement, gate-evidence, and cross-document completion oracles.

Reviewed retirement and migration coverage plus consolidated runtime wiring, Goal commands, and the planning approval-to-build chain. Bridge retirement is clear, while distributed precedence and command lifecycle, concurrency, partial-failure, and recovery matrices remain insufficiently falsifiable.

Reviewed notification and sound wiring, Usage correlation routing, production wiring repair, onboarding routes, and DRY settings propagation. Anti-fabrication wiring rules are strong; credential and delivery recovery, sensitive-reference authorization, interrupted onboarding routes, and setting-projection convergence need explicit adversarial contracts.

Which privacy and authorization contract governs passthrough and display of raw_payload_ref, receipt refs, trace_ref, and provider_attempt_ref in Usage routes?
